statement: Whenever sorted_list_to_bst head = Result.ok T, the tree T is a height-balanced binary search tree whose in-order traversal equals vals(head). Define inorder(Tree.Null)=[] and inorder(Tree.Node(x,L,R))=inorder(L)++[x]++inorder(R). T is a binary search tree iff for every subtree Tree.Node(x,L,R) occurring in T, every element of inorder(L) is <= x and every element of inorder(R) is >= x. Define height(Tree.Null)=0 and height(Tree.Node(_,L,R))=1+max(height(L),height(R)). T is height-balanced iff for every subtree Tree.Node(_,L,R) occurring in T, |height(L)-height(R)| <= 1.
preconditions: Let len(head) be the number of nodes in the linked list head. Let vals(head) be the sequence of values of head read from the first node to the last. The list head satisfies: 0 <= len(head) <= 20000; every value in vals(head) is in [-100000, 100000]; and vals(head) is non-decreasing (sorted in ascending order, duplicates allowed).
